threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand bewildered at the number of local coffee shops, trying to choose between flat whites and oat lattes like it’s life or death.
Caught a glimpse of a guy on the night bus perfectly balancing a half-eaten kebab while chatting up a girl. Only in Deptford, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: It hit me when I spotted the same dog in a beret every morning at the corner bakery. That quirky routine made it feel like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's late-night Döner shops serve their kebabs with curry powder—never seen that in Istanbul or anywhere else. Totally Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You notice they call it 'the Mission' not 'the Mission District' and can name three taquerias that aren't on tourist lists.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy making a origami crane from a bus transfer while his toddler watched, totally unbothered by the chaos around him. Classic Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think they can just stroll into a local bar and order a 'tapa' without knowing it's actually a 'pica-pica' in our part of town.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still navigate the metro with a paper map, oblivious to the efficiency of Google Maps—classic sign of a newbie in Gràcia.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still check the tube app like it's a crystal ball; locals know the bus is faster half the time.
Saw a couple on the bus last night arguing over who left the milk out. By the time we hit Stockwell, they had swapped to sharing a bag of chips.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a group of kids argue over which Döner spot had the spiciest sauce, and they were serious about it. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, you'll find spontaneous open-air cinema events in parks—projecting classics on blankets under the stars. It's pure Berlin magic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows the difference between a BART delay and a BART meltdown. The eye roll when the Civic Center station closed? Classic.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading commuters at the Civic Center stop with a ukulele while the bus was delayed. Crowd loved it, even with the chaos around.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists assume we all drink sangria at the corner bars—most locals prefer a cervecita at home or a quiet vermut in the plaza.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they navigate the metro—still clutching a paper map and fumbling with the ticket machines.
